overview_markdown:
NullClaw is a ground-up reimagining of autonomous AI assistant infrastructure written entirely in Zig. It ships as a 678 KB static binary with no runtime, VM, or framework overhead, peaking at roughly 1 MB RSS and booting in under 2 ms on Apple Silicon (under 8 ms on a 0.8 GHz edge core). Despite the tiny footprint it is feature-complete: 50+ LLM providers, 19 chat channels, 35+ tools, 10 memory engines, MCP support, subagents, streaming, voice, tunnels, and hardware peripherals.

Architecturally, everything is a vtable interface — providers, channels, tools, memory, tunnels, and peripherals are all pluggable and swappable. Security is a first-class concern: pairing-based auth, multi-layer sandboxing via landlock, firejail, bubblewrap, or Docker, explicit allowlists, workspace scoping, and encrypted secrets. Recent commits show active hardening work, including memory-safety fixes (use-after-free in cron delivery), secure HTTP fallbacks on Android, and careful diagnostics logging with redacted, truncated payloads.

Compared to OpenClaw, NullClaw targets the opposite end of the spectrum: instead of a rich skill registry and Control UI, it bets on minimalism, portability, and auditability. The surrounding Null ecosystem (nullhub UI, nullboiler orchestration, nullwatch observability, nulltickets task tracking) is emerging but still beta. Ecosystem digests characterize it as a low-velocity, quiet-maintenance project, so it suits users who prioritize footprint and control over community momentum.
